models.name: Droplet flame goes out (FLEX)
models.question: Will a burning fuel droplet's flame go out on its own before the fuel is used up?
models.data: NASA FLEX, PSI-69 (doi:10.60555/mbq8-0451): 260 methanol and n-heptane droplet burns on the ISS, 0.69-3.05 atm, 12%-34% O2, up to 70% CO2 or 45% He added, initial diameter 1.1-4.7 mm. Outcome: NASA's 'Test end' = Extinction (vs Disruption or Completion).
models.method: Model chosen inside every training split from: logistic regression on the raw inputs with fuel interactions; logistic regression on physics features (inert heat capacity per O2, O2 partial pressure, gas conductivity); Gaussian-process classifier. Picked: LR physics features (C=10) 69%, Gaussian-process classifier 15%, LR raw+fuel interactions (C=10) 14%, LR physics features (C=0.1) 1%, LR raw+fuel interactions (C=1) 1%.
models.validation: Whole test sessions held out: 5-fold grouped by ISS test date (80 dates), repeated 20 times. Score = median AUC; range = 95% session bootstrap.

models.limits: Microgravity droplets only (two fuels, 1.1-4.7 mm). NASA does not define 'Test end' publicly; with Disruption burns dropped the AUC is 0.89, and with whole atmospheres held out it is 0.90. The FLEX plan aimed at near-limit conditions, so the chance shown is for those conditions, not for cabin fires in general. A low chance of extinction does not make an atmosphere safe, and nothing here applies to Moon or Mars gravity.

models.name: Droplet burning rate (FLEX)
models.question: How fast does a burning fuel droplet shrink, in this atmosphere?
models.data: NASA FLEX, PSI-69 (doi:10.60555/mbq8-0451): 256 methanol and n-heptane droplet burns with a measured burning-rate constant K = -d(D^2)/dt.
models.method: Textbook d-squared law (K proportional to gas conductivity/heat capacity times ln(1+B), constants from NIST, one scale factor per fuel) multiplied by a learned correction chosen inside every training split. Picked: d2 law x ridge (alpha=10) 100%.
models.validation: Whole test sessions held out: 5-fold grouped by ISS test date (80 dates), repeated 20 times. Score = median MAE; range = 95% session bootstrap.

models.name: Burns on invisibly after the flame goes out (CFI)
models.question: After the visible flame goes out, does a cool flame keep the droplet burning until all the fuel is used up?
models.data: NASA CFI, PSI-39 (doi:10.60555/m6pj-a914): 117 n-dodecane and n-dodecane/iso-dodecane droplet burns (3.9-6.4 mm) whose visible flame went out and then burned on as a cool flame, 0.5-5 atm, 17%-21% O2, 0-59% He. Gas flames (CFI-G, PSI-159): cool flames were seen only with 30% n-butane and 40% O2 at 2.03 bar.
models.method: Logistic regression on pressure, O2, helium, droplet size, fuel blend and support fibre; strength chosen inside every training split. Label: 'Dext,cool' = 0 in NASA's analysis (droplet used up) versus a cool flame that went out and left fuel.
models.validation: Whole test sessions held out: 5-fold grouped by ISS test date (39 dates), repeated 20 times. Score = median AUC; range = 95% session bootstrap.
models.unit: chance the droplet is used up (0-1)
